=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## A preliminary point on the Seller's framing

The covering note says these positions are "standard and widely accepted market terms", were "settled at principal level", and are "FINAL and not intended to be re-opened." That is advocacy, not agreement. Two things follow:

1. **Confirm with Wattlebridge's principals** whether any of these points were actually agreed. Nothing in the documents evidences agreement. Several positions, such as capping title warranties and applying limitations to fraud, are not market for a buyer in any version I would recognise.
2. **Some figures sit at the edge of the range the Seller cites, and some go outside it.** The cap is at the top end, at 20%. The basket is a deductible, not a tipping basket. Fundamental warranties and fraud are swept in.

The deal is 100% of shares for AUD 24m, debt-free/cash-free, under NSW law. The analysis below is framed against that baseline.

---

## Part 1: Liability regime

### 1. Limitations applied to "all Claims" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
This is the most consequential drafting point in the package. The Seller wants every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance clause to apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise." As drafted, that would cap and time-bar:
- title and capacity claims
- tax claims
- specific indemnities (Ironquay, and anything we add for DD-006)
- price adjustments and leakage
- fraud

**Push back:**
- Limitations should apply to **general Warranty Claims only**, with each other category given its own regime.
- Add an express **carve-out for fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment** by the Seller, the Company or their representatives. No cap, basket, time limit or knowledge exclusion should apply to these.
- Non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses must not exclude fraud claims. Under Australian law, liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 ACL cannot be fully contracted out of. Don't let the drafting imply otherwise.

### 2. General cap: 20% / AUD 4.8m (cl 12.1)
20% is at the top of the Seller's own quoted range. On its own it is not unreasonable for general warranties. However, the known exposures disclosed below include Bluefen (30% of revenue), Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), the Ironquay IP title gap and the privacy incident. In that context, 20% only works if those items sit **outside** the cap.

**Position:**
- Accept around 20–30% for general warranties only, and only if W&I insurance is not being used.
- Fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims should sit outside the cap (see items 4–5).
- If a W&I policy is being considered, address it now. It changes the cap and retention analysis.

### 3. De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k as a deductible (cl 12.2)
- **The basket structure is the main problem.** It is about 1.04% of price, and "only the excess is recoverable" makes it a deductible. Push for a **tipping basket**: once the threshold is reached, recovery runs from the first dollar.
- **Make de minimis claims aggregate.** Claims arising from the same or related facts should count together toward the de minimis. Claims below de minimis should still count toward the basket.
- Consider negotiating de minimis down to around AUD 10–15k and the basket down to about 0.5–0.75%.
- Fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, leakage and fraud claims should be excluded from both thresholds.

### 4. Title and capacity subject to general caps and time limits ("administrative simplicity")
**Reject outright.** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing. The market position is:
- cap at **100% of price**
- time limit of about **6–7 years**, or the statutory limitation period
- no basket or de minimis
- no disclosure against these warranties

### 5. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
Neither was settled as far as the documents show.
- **Tax:** use a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation guarantee (see item 10). The time limit should be about 5–7 years, consistent with ATO amendment periods. The cap should be up to 100% of price, with no basket.
- **IP:** the Company's value depends on its IP, and there is a known title gap (Ironquay). IP ownership warranties should carry an extended time limit (e.g. 3–4 years) and an elevated cap. The Ironquay matter needs its own indemnity (item 11).

### 6. 18-month general time limit (cl 12.3)
This is within market range. Accept it for **general warranties only**, provided:
- the period covers at least one full audit cycle after Completion
- the notification requirements (content and follow-up proceedings) are not unduly onerous.

---

## Part 2: Disclosure and knowledge

### 7. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2, Sch 7)
Read together with the knowledge clause, this would hollow out most warranties. Anything buried anywhere in the data room or on any public register would defeat a claim.

**Push back:**
- **Delete general disclosure of the data room.** At most, allow disclosure of specifically identified documents.
- Allow public-register disclosure only for searches actually conducted and listed, as at a stated date.
- Adopt a **"fairly disclosed" standard**: disclosed with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter.
- **Fundamental and tax warranties should not be qualified by disclosure.**
- **Bring the disclosure date forward.** The letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, six weeks ago. Require an agreed, certified data room index (e.g. on USB) and an updated position. Any supplementary disclosure before Completion should not cure breach. Instead it should give the Buyer a right to terminate or claim.

### 8. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)
**Reject.** It covers the knowledge of "the Buyer or its advisers" and anything "discoverable", which is constructive knowledge. This is especially dangerous here because we already know about the problem items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses). Under this clause, every protection we negotiate for those items could be argued away.

**Positions, in order of preference:**
1. Express **pro-sandbagging**: Buyer knowledge does not limit claims.
2. Silence.
3. Fallback: only the *actual* knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. No advisers, no constructive knowledge. Specific indemnities and fundamental, tax and fraud claims must be carved out in all cases.

---

## Part 3: Specific commercial issues

### 9. Bluefen change-of-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL item 2)
Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or around 30% of FY26 revenue, so losing it would seriously damage the business case. The Disclosure Letter confirms that **no final written consent exists and there is no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.** The Seller wants only reasonable endeavours, with the condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **condition precedent for the Buyer's sole benefit**, waivable only by the Buyer.
- The condition should require **unconditional written consent** (or consent on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), with **all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied**, no adverse change to contract terms, and no notice of termination or non-renewal.
- Upgrade the Seller's obligation to **all reasonable endeavours**, with the Buyer having approval rights over the approach to Bluefen.
- Agree a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right. As a fallback, consider a price adjustment or deferred consideration if Bluefen terminates within a set period after Completion.
- Request the DD-002 cl 11.2–11.3 wording urgently. The CP must track it exactly.

### 10. Riverlark facility, about AUD 3.2m (cl 2 / 7; DL item 3)
A "release to be provided following Completion" is **inconsistent with the debt-free basis** and leaves the Company in default under change-control cl 8.1 from the moment of Completion.

**Push back:**
- Treat it as **Debt deducted from price**, paid directly to Riverlark from completion funds.
- Completion deliverables should include:
  - a signed **payout letter** with a daily figure
  - a **deed of release**
  - executed **PPSR financing change statements** (or an undertaking to lodge them immediately, with authority for the Buyer to lodge)
  - return of any title documents.
- Add a specific indemnity for any amount that remains outstanding.

### 11. DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 ("a matter for the Seller")
The Company, not the Seller, is the employer, so the liability lands on the Company and therefore on the Buyer after Completion. The Disclosure Letter is silent on payroll tax, super and other on-costs.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses as **Transaction Costs / Debt**, deducted from price and itemised in the funds flow.
- **Gross the deduction up** for employer payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, workers' compensation and any other on-costs.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including amounts that become payable later (e.g. deferred tranches tied to continued employment). Exclude this indemnity from the cap, basket and knowledge exclusion.

### 12. Ironquay IP indemnity "limited to SOW3 payment" (cl 11.1; DL item 4)
The real risk is **title to the SOW3 Project Materials**. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, there is no receipt, and there is no confirmatory assignment. Paying AUD 180k does not by itself fix the title gap, and an indemnity limited to that payment does not cover what actually goes wrong if title has not passed. That could include:
- third-party infringement claims
- injunctions
- the cost of re-engineering
- customer claims.

**Push back:**
- **CP or completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment, plus a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay, including moral rights consents where relevant.
- If the AUD 180k is unpaid at Completion, treat it as Debt.
- Add a broad **specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials. Exclude it from the general cap, basket and knowledge exclusion, with an extended time limit.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident ("preliminary operational matter")
About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are all unresolved as at 22 September. Under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the Company must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days. By today, 5 November, that assessment should be complete. If it is not, that is itself a compliance concern.

**Push back / actions:**
- **Request now** the assessment outcome, the decision on whether to notify the OAIC and affected individuals, the forensic report, and any customer contractual notifications (check the Bluefen and other customer DPAs).
- Add a **specific indemnity** for all Loss from the incident: regulatory, remediation, notification, customer claims and contractual penalties. It should sit outside the general cap and basket (or under a separate dedicated cap) and be unaffected by disclosure or knowledge.
- Add pre-Completion covenants: complete the investigation, comply with the NDB scheme, and give the Buyer consultation rights over notifications.
- Require a warranty that no other incidents have occurred.

### 14. Sandbar renewals: 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 ("ordinary course")
The Disclosure Letter says these are related renewals to be "read together for timing/scope." Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three equal tranches is a classic way to stay **under a materiality or conduct-of-business threshold**. Check the SPA's material contract definition and interim-period consent threshold. If either sits above AUD 110k but below AUD 330k, that strongly suggests the split was used to avoid it.

**Push back:**
- Request the contracts, dates, term, termination rights and whether the amounts are prepaid or accrued.
- Aggregate related contracts for the purposes of all thresholds.
- If entered or renewed in the interim period without consent, or if not genuinely ordinary course, treat them as **Leakage / Debt**, or require termination at the Seller's cost.
- Ensure the amounts are correctly reflected in the working capital or completion accounts.

### 15. Title evidenced by the share register (DD-012; DL item 10)
A register entry is not sufficient. The register can be wrong, and it says nothing about encumbrances or options.

**Push back:**
- Require **unqualified title warranties**: legal and beneficial ownership, fully paid, free of Encumbrances, and no options, convertibles or rights to issue shares.
- Cross-check against **ASIC records** and the PPSR (a Riverlark security over the shares is possible).
- Completion deliverables should include share certificates (or lost certificate indemnities), signed transfers, and releases of any security over the shares.
- No disclosure against title (see item 4).

### 16. Lower-risk items: lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- **Lease:** make the landlord notification a completion deliverable or post-Completion covenant, and confirm there is no change-of-control consent requirement.
- **Mossvale:** confirm the definition of "assignment" in DD-009 does not deem a change of control to be an assignment. Obtain a warranty that no consents are needed beyond those listed.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scope of limitations | Applies to all Claims, including fraud | General warranties only; carve out fraud, title, tax, indemnities, leakage | **Critical** |
| 4 | Title/capacity | Same cap and time limit as general | 100% of price, 6–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure | **Critical** |
| 7 | General disclosure | Whole data room plus public registers | Specific, fair disclosure only; agreed index; no disclosure against fundamentals | **Critical** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Buyer and advisers; anything discoverable | Delete or pro-sandbag; fallback is actual knowledge of named individuals | **Critical** |
| 9 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied | Buyer-only CP; unconditional consent; cl 11.3 satisfied; long-stop | **Critical** |
| 10 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Debt deducted; payout, deed of release and PPSR at Completion | **Critical** |
| 12 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment; full IP indemnity | **High** |
| 13 | DD-006 privacy | "Preliminary, not material" | Current NDB status; uncapped/separate specific indemnity; covenants | **High** |
| 11 | Bonuses AUD 420k | "Matter for Seller"; not in funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Cost, grossed up for on-costs; indemnity | **High** |
| 5 | Tax/IP | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity (5–7 years); enhanced IP warranties | **High** |
| 3 | Basket/de minimis | AUD 250k deductible; AUD 25k | Tipping basket; aggregate related claims; lower thresholds | Medium |
| 14 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Full details; aggregate for thresholds; Leakage/Debt if not ordinary course | Medium |
| 15 | Title evidence | Share register only | Unqualified warranties; ASIC/PPSR checks; completion deliverables | Medium |
| 2, 6 | Cap 20%; 18 months | As proposed | Broadly acceptable for **general warranties only**, if the carve-outs are agreed | Medium |
| 16 | Lease/Mossvale | Notification/assignment only | Confirm; deliverable or covenant | Low |

### Suggested next steps
1. **Check with our principals** whether any point was in fact agreed at principal level, before we respond to the "FINAL" framing.
2. **Send an urgent information request** covering:
   - DD-006 NDB assessment status
   - Bluefen cl 11.2–11.3 wording and consent status
   - Riverlark payout figure and security details, including whether there is any share security
   - Ironquay payment evidence
   - the Sandbar contracts
   - DD-005 bonus terms and on-cost calculation.
3. **Restructure price mechanics.** Riverlark, the bonuses (grossed up) and any unpaid Ironquay fees become Debt or Transaction Costs in the funds flow. That moves them out of the warranty regime altogether.
4. **Decide on W&I insurance.** If it is being used, it reshapes the cap and retention points, but known matters (items 9–14) will be excluded from cover and still need specific indemnities from the Seller.
5. **Prepare the mark-up**, leading with the critical items above.

This is a review of the Seller's summary positions and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA text. Each point should be confirmed against the actual clause wording and the defined terms (Claims, Debt, Leakage, Encumbrance, Material Contract) once we have the full draft.

- Add a specific indemnity for any amount that remains outstanding.

### 11. DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 ("a matter for the Seller")
The Company, not the Seller, is the employer, so the liability lands on the Company and therefore on the Buyer after Completion. The Disclosure Letter is silent on payroll tax, super and other on-costs.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses as **Transaction Costs / Debt**, deducted from price and itemised in the funds flow.
- **Gross the deduction up** for employer payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, workers' compensation and any other on-costs.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including amounts that become payable later (e.g. deferred tranches tied to continued employment). Exclude this indemnity from the cap, basket and knowledge exclusion.

### 12. Ironquay IP indemnity "limited to SOW3 payment" (cl 11.1; DL item 4)
The real risk is **title to the SOW3 Project Materials**. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, there is no receipt, and there is no confirmatory assignment. Paying AUD 180k does not by itself fix the title gap, and an indemnity limited to that payment does not cover what actually goes wrong if title has not passed. That could include:
- third-party infringement claims
- injunctions
- the cost of re-engineering
- customer claims.

**Push back:**
- **CP or completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment, plus a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay, including moral rights consents where relevant.
- If the AUD 180k is unpaid at Completion, treat it as Debt.
- Add a broad **specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials. Exclude it from the general cap, basket and knowledge exclusion, with an extended time limit.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident ("preliminary operational matter")
About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are all unresolved as at 22 September. Under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the Company must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days. By today, 5 November, that assessment should be complete. If it is not, that is itself a compliance concern.

**Push back / actions:**
- **Request now** the assessment outcome, the decision on whether to notify the OAIC and affected individuals, the forensic report, and any customer contractual notifications (check the Bluefen and other customer DPAs).
- Add a **specific indemnity** for all Loss from the incident: regulatory, remediation, notification, customer claims and contractual penalties. It should sit outside the general cap and basket (or under a separate dedicated cap) and be unaffected by disclosure or knowledge.
- Add pre-Completion covenants: complete the investigation, comply with the NDB scheme, and give the Buyer consultation rights over notifications.
- Require a warranty that no other incidents have occurred.

### 14. Sandbar renewals: 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 ("ordinary course")
The Disclosure Letter says these are related renewals to be "read together for timing/scope." Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three equal tranches is a classic way to stay **under a materiality or conduct-of-business threshold**. Check the SPA's material contract definition and interim-period consent threshold. If either sits above AUD 110k but below AUD 330k, that strongly suggests the split was used to avoid it.

**Push back:**
- Request the contracts, dates, term, termination rights and whether the amounts are prepaid or accrued.
- Aggregate related contracts for the purposes of all thresholds.
- If entered or renewed in the interim period without consent, or if not genuinely ordinary course, treat them as **Leakage / Debt**, or require termination at the Seller's cost.
- Ensure the amounts are correctly reflected in the working capital or completion accounts.

### 15. Title evidenced by the share register (DD-012; DL item 10)
A register entry is not sufficient. The register can be wrong, and it says nothing about encumbrances or options.

**Push back:**
- Require **unqualified title warranties**: legal and beneficial ownership, fully paid, free of Encumbrances, and no options, convertibles or rights to issue shares.
- Cross-check against **ASIC records** and the PPSR (a Riverlark security over the shares is possible).
- Completion deliverables should include share certificates (or lost certificate indemnities), signed transfers, and releases of any security over the shares.
- No disclosure against title (see item 4).

### 16. Lower-risk items: lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- **Lease:** make the landlord notification a completion deliverable or post-Completion covenant, and confirm there is no change-of-control consent requirement.
- **Mossvale:** confirm the definition of "assignment" in DD-009 does not deem a change of control to be an assignment. Obtain a warranty that no consents are needed beyond those listed.
